claim: SOX2 positive pituitary stem cells (PSCs) are specified embryonically and persist throughout life, giving rise to all pituitary endocrine lineages.
source: SOX2 positive pituitary stem cells (PSCs) are specified embryonically and persist throughout life, giving rise to all pituitary endocrine lineages.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous work (Andoniadou et al., 2013; Rizzoti et al., 2013) as referenced in the Introduction section.

claim: The activation of the STK/LATS/YAP/TAZ signalling cascade has been previously shown in the developing and postnatal mammalian pituitary.
source: We have previously shown the activation of the STK/LATS/YAP/TAZ signalling cascade in the developing and postnatal mammalian pituitary.
evidence: This is a reference to the authors' previous work, as indicated by 'We have previously shown'.

claim: Restricting YAP/TAZ activation during development is essential for normal organ size and specification from SOX2+ PSCs.
source: Through loss- and gain-of-function genetic approaches, we reveal that restricting YAP/TAZ activation during development is essential for normal organ size and specification from SOX2+ PSCs.
evidence: This claim is supported by the genetic experiments described in the manuscript, including embryonic phenotypes shown in Figures 1 and 2.

claim: Postnatal deletion of LATS kinases and subsequent upregulation of YAP/TAZ leads to uncontrolled clonal expansion of the SOX2+ PSCs and disruption of their differentiation, causing the formation of non-secreting, aggressive pituitary tumours.
source: Postnatal deletion of LATS kinases and subsequent upregulation of YAP/TAZ leads to uncontrolled clonal expansion of the SOX2+ PSCs and disruption of their differentiation, causing the formation of non-secreting, aggressive pituitary tumours.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from postnatal LATS deletion experiments shown in Figures 3 and 4.

claim: Sustained expression of YAP alone results in expansion of SOX2+ PSCs capable of differentiation and devoid of tumourigenic potential.
source: In contrast, sustained expression of YAP alone results in expansion of SOX2+ PSCs capable of differentiation and devoid of tumourigenic potential.
evidence: This claim is supported by the YAP-TetO experiments described in Figure 5.

claim: The LATS/YAP/TAZ signalling cascade is an essential component of PSC regulation in normal pituitary physiology and tumourigenesis.
source: Our findings identify the LATS/YAP/TAZ signalling cascade as an essential component of PSC regulation in normal pituitary physiology and tumourigenesis.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on all the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The pituitary gland is composed of three parts: the anterior, intermediate and posterior lobes (AL, IL and PL, respectively).
source: The pituitary gland is composed of three parts, the anterior, intermediate and posterior lobes (AL, IL and PL, respectively).
evidence: This is established anatomical knowledge about pituitary structure.

claim: The AL and IL contain hormone-secreting cells, which are derived from an evagination of the oral ectoderm expressing SOX2, termed Rathke's pouch (RP).
source: The AL and IL contain hormone-secreting cells, which are derived from an evagination of the oral ectoderm expressing SOX2, termed Rathke's pouch (RP).
evidence: This is established developmental biology knowledge about pituitary development.

claim: SOX2+ cells in the embryonic and adult pituitary can differentiate into three endocrine cell lineages marked by transcription factors PIT1 (POU1F1), TPIT (TBX19) and SF1 (NR5A1).
source: SOX2+ cells, both in the embryonic and adult pituitary, can differentiate into three endocrine cell lineages, which are marked by transcription factors PIT1 (POU1F1) (Li et al., 1990), TPIT (TBX19) (Pulichino et al., 2003) and SF1 (NR5A1) (Ingraham et al., 1994)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous work establishing these lineage markers.

claim: SOX2+ PSCs are highly proliferative during the first 2–3 weeks of life, in concordance with major organ growth.
source: SOX2+ PSCs are highly proliferative during the first 2–3 weeks of life, in concordance with major organ growth, after which they reach a steady low proliferative capacity that contributes to maintain normal homeostasis and physiological adaptation of the pituitary gland (Levy, 2002; Nolan et al., 1998).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies on pituitary stem cell proliferation.

claim: Pituitary tumours represent 10–15% of all intracranial neoplasms.
source: Pituitary tumours are common in the population, representing 10–15% of all intracranial neoplasms (Bronstein et al., 2011; Daly et al., 2006).
evidence: This epidemiological claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Targeting oncogenic beta-catenin in SOX2+ PSCs in the mouse generates clusters of senescent SOX2+ cells that induce tumours resembling ACP in a paracrine manner.
source: Targeting oncogenic beta-catenin in SOX2+ PSCs in the mouse generates clusters of senescent SOX2+ cells that induce tumours resembling ACP in a paracrine manner, that is the tumours do not derive from the targeted SOX2+ PSCs (Andoniadou et al., 2013; Gonzalez-Meljem et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous work by the authors.

claim: Up to 15% of adenomas and 50% of ACP display aggressive behaviour with invasion of nearby structures including the hypothalamus and visual tracts.
source: Up to 15% of adenomas and 50% of ACP display aggressive behaviour with invasion of nearby structures including the hypothalamus and visual tracts, associated with significant morbidity and mortality (Lasolle et al., 2017).
evidence: This clinical claim is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: The Hippo pathway controls stem cell proliferation and tumourigenesis in several organs such as in the liver, intestines and lung.
source: The Hippo pathway controls stem cell proliferation and tumourigenesis in several organs such as in the liver (Zhou et al., 2009; Lu et al., 2018), intestines (Zhou et al., 2011) and lung (Lin et al., 2015; Nantie et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to previous work on the Hippo pathway in different organs.

claim: STK3/4 kinases phosphorylate and activate LATS1/2 serine/threonine-protein kinases in the core phosphorylation cascade.
source: In the core phosphorylation cascade, STK3/4 kinases phosphorylate and activate LATS1/2 serine/threonine-protein kinases, which in turn phosphorylate co-activators Yes-associated protein (YAP1, a.k.a. YAP) and WW domain-containing transcription regulator protein 1 (WWTR1, a.k.a. TAZ) that are subsequently inactivated through degradation and cytoplasmic retention (Meng et al., 2016).
evidence: This mechanistic claim is supported by citation to previous work on the Hippo pathway.

claim: Active YAP/TAZ associate with TEAD transcription factors, promoting the transcription of target genes such as Cyr61 and Ctgf.
source: Active YAP/TAZ associate with TEAD transcription factors, promoting the transcription of target genes such as Cyr61 and Ctgf (Zhao et al., 2008; Zhang et al., 2009; Zhou et al., 2016).
evidence: This mechanistic claim is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: YAP/TAZ have been shown to promote proliferation and the stem cell state in several organs.
source: YAP/TAZ have been shown to promote proliferation and the stem cell state in several organs, and can also lead to transformation and tumour initiation when overexpressed (Camargo et al., 2007; Schlegelmilch et al., 2011; Dong et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous work on YAP/TAZ function.

claim: Strong nuclear localisation of YAP and TAZ was observed exclusively in SOX2+ stem cells of developing Rathke's pouch and the postnatal anterior pituitary of mice and humans.
source: We previously reported strong nuclear localisation of YAP and TAZ exclusively in SOX2+ stem cells of developing Rathke's pouch and the postnatal anterior pituitary of mice and humans, and enhanced expression in human pituitary tumours composed of uncommitted cells, including ACPs and null-cell adenomas (Lodge et al., 2016; Xekouki et al., 2019)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to the authors' previous work.

claim: Phosphorylation of YAP at serine 127 (S127) was detected in SOX2+ populations, indicating LATS kinase activity.
source: In these populations we detected phosphorylation of YAP at serine 127 (S127) indicating LATS kinase activity.
evidence: This is based on the authors' previous observations and knowledge of YAP phosphorylation as a marker of LATS activity.

claim: Accumulation of total YAP protein but not of TAZ or pYAP(S127) was observed throughout the developing pituitary and hypothalamus of YAP-TetO embryos at 15.5dpc.
source: As expected, we confirmed accumulation of total YAP protein but not of TAZ or pYAP(S127), throughout the developing pituitary and hypothalamus of Hesx1Cre/+;R26rtTA/+;Col1a1tetO-Yap/+ (hereafter YAP-TetO) embryos at 15.5dpc, but not of Cre-negative controls (Figure 1B, Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The YAP downstream target Cyr61 was upregulated in YAP-TetO embryos.
source: Likewise, the YAP downstream target Cyr61 (Figure 1B) was also upregulated.
evidence: This claim is supported by RNAscope data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: YAP-TetO mutants displayed a dysplastic anterior pituitary, which was more medially compacted and lacked a central lumen.
source: Morphologically, YAP-TetO mutants displayed a dysplastic anterior pituitary, which was more medially compacted and lacked a central lumen, making it difficult to distinguish between the developing anterior and intermediate lobes (Figure 1C).
evidence: This morphological observation is supported by histological data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Mutant pituitaries had abundant SOX2 positive cells in the most lateral regions at 15.5dpc, whereas control pituitaries showed loss of SOX2 in these regions.
source: Immunofluorescence staining against SOX2 at 15.5dpc demonstrated loss of SOX2 in the most lateral regions of control pituitaries (arrows in Figure 1C), where cells are undergoing commitment; yet mutant pituitaries had abundant SOX2 positive cells in the most lateral regions (arrowheads in Figure 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: YAP-TetO mutants showed a concomitant reduction in committed cell lineages throughout the gland at 15.5dpc.
source: Staining using antibodies against lineage markers PIT1, TPIT and SF1 revealed a concomitant reduction in committed cell lineages throughout the gland (Figure 1D; PIT1 0.35% in mutants compared with 30.21% in controls (Student's t-test p<0.0001, n = 3 for each genotype), TPIT 1.03% in mutants compared with 9.81% in controls (Student's t-test p=0.0012, n = 3 for each genotype), SF1 0.34% in mutants compared with 4.14% in controls (Student's t-test p=0.0021, n = 3 for each genotype)).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantified immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Sustained activation of YAP prevents lineage commitment and is sufficient to maintain the progenitor state during embryonic development.
source: We therefore conclude that sustained activation of YAP prevents lineage commitment and is sufficient to maintain the progenitor state during embryonic development.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data on YAP-TetO embryos.

claim: No live Hesx1Cre/+;R26rtTA/+;Col1a1tetO-Yap/+ pups were obtained at birth when treated with doxycycline from 5.5dpc (n = 5 litters).
source: We did not obtain any live Hesx1Cre/+;R26rtTA/+;Col1a1tetO-Yap/+ pups at birth when treated with doxycycline from 5.5dpc (n = 5 litters).
evidence: This is an observation from breeding experiments.

claim: Hesx1Cre/+;R26rtTA/+;Col1a1tetO-Yap/+ pups treated with doxycycline from 9.5dpc were viable but reached an experimental end point at P24 due to excessive weight loss.
source: Hesx1Cre/+;R26rtTA/+;Col1a1tetO-Yap/+ pups were viable and were maintained on doxycycline until P24, at which point the experimental end point was reached due to excessive weight loss and animals had to be culled following UK Home Office Regulations.
evidence: This is an observation from the experimental protocol.

claim: Histological analyses of YAP-TetO pituitaries at P24 revealed multiple anterior lobe cysts per gland, localising predominantly in the ventral AL (n = 4).
source: Histological analyses of pituitaries revealed multiple anterior lobe cysts per gland, localising predominantly in the ventral AL (n = 4) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by histological data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Cystic structures in YAP-TetO mutants developed in YAP-accumulating regions and were lined by SOX2+ cells.
source: These structures developed in YAP-accumulating regions and were lined by SOX2+ cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1D.

claim: The proportion of SOX2+ cells throughout the AL was increased in YAP-TetO mutants at P24.
source: The proportion of SOX2+ cells throughout the AL was increased, as was the percentage of SF1+ cells, whereas PIT1+ cell numbers were significantly decreased and differentiated cells of the TPIT lineage, identified by ACTH antibody staining, were unaffected (Figure 1—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantified immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1E.

claim: Cysts in YAP-TetO mutants were lined by cytokeratin+ cells using the AE1/AE3 pan-cytokeratin cocktail and basal cells were positive for nuclear p63.
source: Immunostaining revealed that cysts were lined by cytokeratin+ cells using the AE1/AE3 pan-cytokeratin cocktail and basal cells were positive for nuclear p63 in Hesx1Cre/+;R26rtTA/+;Col1a1tetO-Yap/+ mutant pituitaries (Figure 1—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1G.

claim: Multi-ciliated cells were observed along the cyst lining in YAP-TetO mutants.
source: Staining using antibodies against ARL13B and Acetylated α-Tubulin (Lys40) marking cilia, revealed multi-ciliated cells along the cyst lining (Figure 1—figure supplement 1H).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1H.

claim: Royal blue-stained mucous cells were detected lining the cysts in YAP-TetO mutants.
source: Combined staining using Alcian Blue and the Periodic Acid-Schiff technique (AB/PAS) to recognise mucins, detected royal blue-stained mucous cells lining the cysts (Figure 1—figure supplement 1H).
evidence: This claim is supported by AB/PAS staining data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1H.

claim: Sustained activation of YAP during embryonic and postnatal pituitary development promotes maintenance and abnormal expansion of SOX2+ epithelia, resulting in the formation of cysts that resemble RCC.
source: Taken together, we conclude that sustained activation of YAP during embryonic and postnatal pituitary development, promotes maintenance and abnormal expansion of SOX2+ epithelia during development, resulting in the formation of cysts that resemble RCC.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data on YAP-TetO mutants.

claim: Hesx1Cre/+;Yapfl/fl;Taz-/- double mutants were obtained at expected ratios during embryonic stages until 15.5dpc.
source: Hesx1Cre/+;Yapfl/fl;Taz-l- double mutants were obtained at expected ratios during embryonic stages until 15.5dpc, however the majority of Taz-/- mutants with or without compound Yap deletions showed lethality at later embryonic and early postnatal stages (Tian et al., 2007) (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by breeding data presented in Supplementary file 1.

claim: The developing pituitary gland of Hesx1Cre/+;Yapfl/fl;Taz-/- double mutants appeared largely normal at 13.5dpc by histology.
source: The developing pituitary gland of Hesx1Cre/+;Yapfl/fl;Taz-l- double mutants appeared largely normal at 13.5dpc by histology (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This claim is supported by histological data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Immunostaining against SOX2 did not reveal differences in the spatial distribution of SOX2+ cells between Hesx1Cre/+;Yapfl/fl;Taz-/- double mutants compared to controls at 13.5dpc, 16.0dpc or P28.
source: Immunostaining against SOX2 to mark embryonic progenitors and postnatal stem cells did not reveal differences in the spatial distribution of SOX2+ cells between double mutants compared to controls (Hesx1+/+;Yapfl/fl;Taz+/+ and Hesx1+/+;Yapfl/fl;Taz+/-) at 13.5dpc, 16.0dpc (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B) or P28, even in regions devoid of both TAZ and active YAP (Figure 1—figure supplement 2C,D).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2B-D.

claim: YAP/TAZ are not required for SOX2+ cell specification or survival.
source: This suggests that YAP/TAZ are not required for SOX2+ cell specification or survival.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the lack of phenotype in YAP/TAZ double mutants.

claim: Analysis of commitment markers PIT1 and SF1 as well as ACTH did not show any differences between Hesx1Cre/+;Yapfl/fl;Taz-/- genotypes and controls.
source: Likewise, analysis of commitment markers PIT1 and SF1 as well as ACTH to identify cells of the TPIT lineage, did not show any differences between genotypes (Figure 1—figure supplement 2E).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2E.

claim: There is no critical requirement for YAP and TAZ during development for the specification of SOX2+ cells or lineage commitment.
source: Together, these data suggest there is no critical requirement for YAP and TAZ during development for the specification of SOX2+ cells or lineage commitment, but that YAP functions to promote the SOX2 cell identity.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the YAP/TAZ deletion experiments.

claim: Conditional deletion of Stk3 and Stk4 in Hesx1Cre/+;Stk3fl/fl;Stk4fl/fl embryos did not lead to a pituitary phenotype.
source: Conditional deletion of Stk3 and Stk4 (also called Mst2 and Mst1) in Hesx1Cre/+;Stk3fl/fl;Stk4fl/fl embryos did not lead to a pituitary phenotype (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: A reduction of over 75% in total STK3/4 proteins in Hesx1Cre/+;Stk3fl/fl;Stk4fl/fl mutants was confirmed by western blot.
source: A reduction of over 75% in total STK3/4 proteins in mutants was confirmed by western blot on total lysates from Hesx1+/+;Stk3fl/fl;Stk4fl/fl controls and Hesx1Cre/+;Stk3fl/fl;Stk4fl/fl mutants (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Hesx1Cre/+;Stk3fl/fl;Stk4fl/fl mutant pituitaries were macroscopically normal at birth.
source: Mutant pituitaries were macroscopically normal at birth (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A), and showed comparable expression patterns of TAZ, YAP, pYAP to controls lacking Cre, without distinct accumulation of YAP or TAZ (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by wholemount and immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A,C.

claim: Normal lineage commitment was evident in Hesx1Cre/+;Stk3fl/fl;Stk4fl/fl mutants by immunofluorescence staining for PIT1, TPIT and SF1 at P10.
source: Normal lineage commitment was evident by immunofluorescence staining for PIT1, TPIT and SF1 at P10 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Hesx1Cre/+;Stk3fl/fl;Stk4fl/fl mutant animals remained healthy and fertile until P70, at which point pituitaries appeared histologically normal.
source: Mutant animals remained healthy and fertile until P70, at which point pituitaries appeared histologically normal (Figure 2—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This claim is supported by histological data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1E.

claim: STK3/4 kinases are not critical for YAP/TAZ regulation in the pituitary.
source: Since deletion of Stk3/4 at embryonic stages does not affect embryonic or postnatal pituitary development, we conclude these kinases are not critical for YAP/TAZ regulation in the pituitary.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the lack of phenotype in STK3/4 deletion mutants.

claim: Hesx1Cre/+;Lats1fl/fl embryos showed unaffected pituitary development and normal localisation and levels of YAP and TAZ.
source: However, Hesx1Cre/+;Lats1fl/fl embryos showed unaffected pituitary development and normal localisation and levels of YAP and TAZ as assessed by immunofluorescence (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A,B) when compared with controls.
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2A,B.

claim: mRNA in situ hybridisation revealed abundant Lats2 transcripts upon conditional deletion of Lats1, suggesting a compensatory upregulation of Lats2 in the absence of LATS1.
source: mRNA in situ hybridisation against Lats2 at P2, revealed abundant Lats2 transcripts upon conditional deletion of Lats1, suggesting a compensatory upregulation of Lats2 in the absence of LATS1 (Figure 2—figure supplement 2C), similar to previous reports of elevated YAP/TAZ signalling inducing Lats2 expression (Moroishi et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNAscope data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2C and citation to previous work.

claim: Deletion of Lats2 alone (Hesx1Cre/+;Lats2fl/fl) did not reveal any developmental morphological anomalies.
source: To overcome potential functional redundancy, we deleted both Lats1 and Lats2 in RP. Deletion of Lats2 alone (Hesx1Cre/+;Lats2fl/fl), did not reveal any developmental morphological anomalies (Figure 2—figure supplement 2D) and pups were identified at normal Mendelian proportions (Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by histological data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2D and breeding data in Supplementary file 2.

claim: Deletion of any three out of four Lats alleles did not affect pituitary development and were identified at normal ratios.
source: Similarly, deletion of any three out of four Lats alleles did not affect pituitary development and were identified at normal ratios, similar to other tissues (Lavado et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by breeding data and citation to previous work.

claim: Homozygous Hesx1Cre/+;Lats1fl/fl;Lats2fl/fl mutants were identified at embryonic stages at reduced Mendelian ratios and were absent at P0-P2, suggesting embryonic and perinatal lethality.
source: Homozygous Hesx1Cre/+;Lats1fl/fl;Lats2fl/fl mutants were identified at embryonic stages at reduced Mendelian ratios and were absent at P0-P2, suggesting embryonic and perinatal lethality (Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by breeding data presented in Supplementary file 2.

claim: Haematoxylin/eosin staining of the developing pituitary gland in Hesx1Cre/+;Lats1fl/fl;Lats2fl/fl mutants revealed overgrowth of RP by 13.5dpc compared to controls (n = 4).
source: Haematoxylin/eosin staining of the developing pituitary gland in Hesx1Cre/+;Lats1fl/fl;Lats2fl/fl mutants revealed overgrowth of RP by 13.5dpc compared to controls lacking Cre (Figure 2A, n = 4).
evidence: This claim is supported by histological data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Total TAZ and YAP proteins accumulated throughout the developing gland in Hesx1Cre/+;Lats1fl/fl;Lats2fl/fl double mutants at 13.5dpc.
source: Total TAZ and YAP proteins accumulated throughout the developing gland in double mutants (arrowheads) but only in the SOX2+ periluminal epithelium of controls (arrows).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The same regions in Hesx1Cre/+;Lats1fl/fl;Lats2fl/fl mutants showed a marked reduction in pYAP-S127 staining at 13.5dpc.
source: The same regions showed a marked reduction in pYAP-S127 staining, which is observed in SOX2+ cells of the control (Figure 2A).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: LATS1/2 normally regulate YAP and TAZ in the pituitary.
source: These findings are in line with LATS1/2 normally regulating YAP and TAZ in the pituitary and demonstrate successful deletion in RP.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the accumulation of YAP/TAZ and loss of pYAP in LATS1/2 mutants.

claim: The Hesx1Cre/+;Lats1fl/fl;Lats2fl/fl mutant pituitary was highly proliferative at 13.5dpc.
source: The mutant pituitary was highly proliferative (Figure 2B, Figure 2—figure supplement 2F; Ki-67 index average 47.42% ± 1.73 SEM in control versus 76.04% ± 9.11 SEM in the double mutant, p=0.0067, Student's t-test)
evidence: This claim is supported by Ki-67 immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2B and quantified in Figure 2—figure supplement 2F.

claim: The majority of cells in Hesx1Cre/+;Lats1fl/fl;Lats2fl/fl mutants expressed SOX2 but not SOX9 at 13.5dpc.
source: and the majority of cells expressed SOX2 (Figure 2A,C) but not SOX9 (Figure 2B, Figure 2—figure supplement 2F).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figures 2A-C.

claim: By 15.5dpc the Hesx1Cre/+;Lats1fl/fl;Lats2fl/fl mutant pituitary was grossly enlarged and exerting a mass effect on the brain, had cysts and displayed areas of necrosis (n = 5).
source: By 15.5dpc the pituitary was grossly enlarged and exerting a mass effect on the brain, had cysts and displayed areas of necrosis (asterisks Figure 2, Figure 2—figure supplement 2E, n = 5).
evidence: This claim is supported by histological data shown in Figure 2 and Figure 2—figure supplement 2E.

claim: Staining for Endomucin revealed poor vascularisation in Hesx1Cre/+;Lats1fl/fl;Lats2fl/fl mutants compared to controls at 15.5dpc.
source: Staining for Endomucin to mark blood vessels revealed poor vascularisation in Hesx1Cre/+;Lats1fl/fl;Lats2fl/fl mutants compared to the ample capillaries seen in the control (Figure 2C), which may account for the necrosis.
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Ectopic residual pituitary tissue was frequently observed at more caudal levels in Hesx1Cre/+;Lats1fl/fl;Lats2fl/fl mutants, reaching the oral epithelium.
source: We frequently observed ectopic residual pituitary tissue at more caudal levels, reaching the oral epithelium and likely interfering with appropriate fusion of the sphenoid, similar to other phenotypes involving pituitary enlargement (arrows Figure 2C) (Andoniadou et al., 2012; Sajedi et al., 2008; Gaston-Massuet et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2C and citations to similar phenotypes.

claim: Immunofluorescence revealed abundant active (non-phosphorylated) YAP throughout the Hesx1Cre/+;Lats1fl/fl;Lats2fl/fl mutant pituitary at 15.5dpc.
source: Immunofluorescence to detect active (non-phosphorylated) YAP revealed abundant staining throughout the pituitary at 15.5dpc, compared to the control where active YAP localises in the SOX2 epithelium (Figure 2C).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Very few cells expressing PIT1, TPIT and SF1 were observed in Hesx1Cre/+;Lats1fl/fl;Lats2fl/fl double mutants at 15.5dpc.
source: Immunofluorescence using specific antibodies against lineage commitment markers PIT1, TPIT and SF1 at 15.5dpc revealed very few cells expressing PIT1, TPIT and SF1 in the double mutant (Figure 2D; PIT1 9.14% in mutants compared with 51.4% in controls (Student's t-test p<0.0001); TPIT 4.0% in mutants compared with 11.4% in controls (Student's t-test p<0.007); SF1 2.1% in mutants compared with 6.5% in controls (Student's t-test p>0.05) n = 3 mutants and five controls), suggesting failure to commit into the three lineages.
evidence: This claim is supported by quantified immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: The LATS/YAP/TAZ axis is required for normal embryonic development of the anterior pituitary.
source: These data suggest that the LATS/YAP/TAZ axis is required for normal embryonic development of the anterior pituitary and that LATS1/2 kinases control proliferation of SOX2+ progenitors and their progression into the three committed lineages.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the LATS1/2 deletion experiments.

claim: LATS1/2 kinases control proliferation of SOX2+ progenitors and their progression into the three committed lineages.
source: These data suggest that the LATS/YAP/TAZ axis is required for normal embryonic development of the anterior pituitary and that LATS1/2 kinases control proliferation of SOX2+ progenitors and their progression into the three committed lineages.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the LATS1/2 deletion experiments showing increased proliferation and reduced commitment.

claim: By P56, all Hesx1Cre/+;Lats1fl/fl pituitaries examined exhibited lesions of abnormal morphology consisting of overgrowths, densely packed nuclei and loss of normal acinar architecture (n = 15).
source: Postnatal analysis of Hesx1Cre/+;Lats1fl/fl pituitaries revealed that by P56, despite developing normally during the embryonic period, all glands examined exhibited lesions of abnormal morphology consisting of overgrowths, densely packed nuclei and loss of normal acinar architecture (n = 15).
evidence: This is an observation from postnatal analysis of LATS1 mutants.

claim: Hesx1Cre/+;Lats1fl/fl;Lats2fl/+ pituitaries developed identifiable lesions accumulating YAP and TAZ at earlier time points (P21 n = 4), the earliest being 10 days.
source: To minimise the likely redundancy by LATS2 seen at embryonic stages, we generated Lats1 mutants additionally haploinsufficient for Lats2 (Hesx1Cre/+;Lats1fl/fl;Lats2fl/+). These pituitaries also developed identifiable lesions accumulating YAP and TAZ (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A), which were observed at earlier time points (P21 n = 4), the earliest being 10 days, indicating increased severity.
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The number of lesions observed per animal was similar between Hesx1Cre/+;Lats1fl/fl and Hesx1Cre/+;Lats1fl/fl;Lats2fl/+ models at P56 (3–8 per animal).
source: The number of lesions observed per animal was similar between the two models at P56 (3–8 per animal).
evidence: This is a quantitative observation from the analysis of both models.

claim: Deletion of Lats2 alone (Hesx1Cre/+;Lats2fl/fl) did not result in any defects.
source: Deletion of Lats2 alone (Hesx1Cre/+;Lats2fl/fl), which is barely expressed in the wild type pituitary, did not result in any defects (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by histological data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Histological examination of Hesx1Cre/+;Lats1fl/fl;Lats2fl/+ pituitaries confirmed the abnormal lesions were tumours, characterised by frequent mitoses, focal necrosis, and a focal squamous differentiation, as well as the occasional presence of cysts.
source: Histological examination of Hesx1Cre/+;Lats1fl/fl;Lats2fl/+ pituitaries confirmed the abnormal lesions were tumours, characterised by frequent mitoses, focal necrosis, and a focal squamous differentiation, as well as the occasional presence of cysts (Figure 3A).
evidence: This claim is supported by histological data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Tumours in Hesx1Cre/+;Lats1fl/fl;Lats2fl/+ pituitaries accumulated YAP/TAZ and upregulated expression of targets Cyr61 and Ctgf.
source: These lesions were identical to those in Hesx1Cre/+;Lats1fl/fl pituitaries (not shown). These tumours accumulated YAP/TAZ and upregulated expression of targets Cyr61 and Ctgf (Figure 3B), confirming the validity of the genetic manipulation (Figure 3B).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence and RNAscope data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Analysis of proliferation by Ki-67 immunostaining revealed an elevated mitotic index of 7–28% in tumours (mean 15.46, SEM ±2.74), compared to 2.97% (SEM ±1.2) mean in control pituitaries.
source: Analysis of proliferation by Ki-67 immunostaining revealed an elevated mitotic index of 7–28% in tumours (mean 15.46, SEM ±2.74), compared to 2.97% (SEM ±1.2) mean in control pituitaries not carrying the Lats1 deletion (Figure 3C).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantified Ki-67 immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The tumours in Hesx1Cre/+;Lats1fl/fl;Lats2fl/+ pituitaries were positive for cytokeratins using AE1/AE3 (multiple keratin cocktail).
source: In keeping with the morphological evidence of epithelial differentiation (Figure 3A), the tumours were positive for cytokeratins using AE1/AE3 (multiple keratin cocktail) (Figure 3—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1E.

claim: The tumours showed focal morphological evidence of squamous differentiation and showed positive nuclear p63 staining.
source: Furthermore, the tumours showed focal morphological evidence of squamous differentiation and showed positive nuclear p63 staining, frequently expressed in squamous carcinomas (Figure 3—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1E.

claim: The tumours did not show immunohistochemical evidence of adenomas, being negative for neuroendocrine markers synaptophysin and neuron-specific enolase.
source: In contrast, the tumours did not show immunohistochemical evidence of adenomas, that is, they were negative for neuroendocrine markers, which all types of adenomas are typically positive for: the neuroendocrine marker synaptophysin and neuron-specific enolase (Figure 3—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1F.

claim: The lesions were negative for chromogranin A, a neuroendocrine granule marker often expressed in clinically non-functioning pituitary adenomas.
source: The lesions were also negative for chromogranin A, a neuroendocrine granule marker often expressed in clinically non-functioning pituitary adenomas.
evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1F.

claim: Tumours were negative for vimentin, expressed by spindle cell oncocytoma, an uncommitted posterior pituitary tumour.
source: Tumours were also negative for vimentin, expressed by spindle cell oncocytoma, an uncommitted posterior pituitary tumour (Figure 3—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1F.

claim: Immunostaining against PIT1, TPIT and SF1 showed only sparse positive cells within the lesions, suggesting lack of commitment into endocrine precursors.
source: Moreover, immunostaining against PIT1, TPIT and SF1 showed only sparse positive cells within the lesions, suggesting lack of commitment into endocrine precursors and supporting the undifferentiated nature of the tumour cells (Figure 3D).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Staining for gamma-H2A.X detected elevated DNA damage in cells of the Hesx1Cre/+;Lats1fl/fl;Lats2fl/+ mutant pituitaries compared with controls.
source: Consistent with a tumourigenic phenotype, and role for LATS1 genomic stabilisation (Pefani et al., 2014), staining for gamma-H2A.X detected elevated DNA damage in cells of the mutant pituitaries compared with controls (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1D and citation to previous work on LATS1 function.

claim: The absence of adenoma or oncocytoma markers together with the histological appearance, observation of focal necrosis and a high mitotic index support the features of squamous carcinoma.
source: The absence of adenoma or oncocytoma markers together with the histological appearance, observation of focal necrosis and a high mitotic index support the features of squamous carcinoma.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the combined histological and immunohistochemical characterization of the tumours.

claim: Tumour regions in Hesx1Cre/+;Lats1fl/fl;Lats2fl/+ pituitaries were mostly composed of SOX2 positive cells (85–97% of cells, 7 tumours across four pituitaries).
source: Tumour regions were mostly composed of SOX2 positive cells, a sub-population of which also expressed SOX9 (Figure 3E, Figure 3—figure supplement 1A; 85–97% of cells, 7 tumours across four pituitaries).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantified immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: Close examination of the marginal zone epithelium revealed a frequent 'ruffling' resembling crypts in Hesx1Cre/+;Lats1fl/fl;Lats2fl/+ mutants.
source: Close examination of the marginal zone epithelium, a major SOX2+ stem cell niche of the pituitary, revealed a frequent 'ruffling' resembling crypts, likely generated through over-proliferation of the epithelial stem cell compartment (Figure 3F).
evidence: This claim is supported by histological and immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3F.

claim: Tamoxifen induction at P5 or P21 in Sox2CreERT2/+;Lats1fl/fl;Lats2fl/+;R26mTmG/+ mice led to abnormal lesions in the anterior pituitary within three months in all cases.
source: Tamoxifen induction at P5 or P21, led to abnormal lesions in the anterior pituitary within three months in all cases.
evidence: This is an observation from the Sox2-CreERT2 lineage tracing experiments.

claim: All animals with tamoxifen induction at P5 developed lesions by P35 in Sox2CreERT2/+;Lats1fl/fl;Lats2fl/+;R26mTmG/+ mice.
source: We focused our analyses on inductions performed at P5, from which time point all animals developed lesions by P35 (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is an observation from the Sox2-CreERT2 lineage tracing experiments shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Lesions in Sox2CreERT2/+;Lats1fl/fl;Lats2fl/+ mice strongly accumulated YAP and TAZ.
source: Similar to observations in Hesx1Cre/+;Lats1fl/fl;Lats2fl/+ animals, these areas strongly accumulated YAP and TAZ (Figure 4B)
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Lesions in Sox2CreERT2/+;Lats1fl/fl;Lats2fl/+ mice activated expression of targets Cyr61 and Ctgf.
source: activated expression of targets Cyr61 and Ctgf
evidence: This claim is supported by RNAscope data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Lesions in Sox2CreERT2/+;Lats1fl/fl;Lats2fl/+ mice displayed ruffling of the AL epithelium.
source: displayed ruffling of the AL epithelium (Figure 4C, Figure 4—figure supplement 1E)
evidence: This claim is supported by RNAscope and histological data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Lesions in Sox2CreERT2/+;Lats1fl/fl;Lats2fl/+ mice lacked lineage commitment markers.
source: and lacked lineage commitment markers (Figure 4D, Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Lesions in Sox2CreERT2/+;Lats1fl/fl;Lats2fl/+ mice showed a similar marker profile to Hesx1-Cre-targeted tumours, with positive p63 and AE1/AE3 staining.
source: These lesions showed a similar marker profile to Hesx1-Cre-targeted tumours, with positive p63 and AE1/AE3 staining (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Lineage tracing confirmed expression of membrane GFP in tumourigenic lesions in Sox2CreERT2/+;Lats1fl/fl;Lats2fl/+;R26mTmG/+ mice, suggesting they were solely derived from SOX2+ cells.
source: Lineage tracing confirmed expression of membrane GFP in tumourigenic lesions, characterised by the accumulation of YAP and expansion of SOX2+ cells, suggesting they were solely derived from SOX2+ cells (Figure 4E, Figure 4—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by lineage tracing data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: LATS kinase activity is required to regulate the pituitary stem cell compartment.
source: Taken together, our data support that LATS kinase activity is required to regulate the pituitary stem cell compartment.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the LATS deletion experiments.

claim: Loss of LATS1 is sufficient to drive deregulation of SOX2+ pituitary stem cells, generating highly proliferative non-functioning tumours with features of carcinomas.
source: Loss of LATS1 is sufficient to drive deregulation of SOX2+ pituitary stem cells, generating highly proliferative non-functioning tumours with features of carcinomas.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the LATS1 deletion experiments and tumour characterization.

claim: No tumours were observed at any stage analysed in YAP-TetO animals treated with doxycycline from P21 to P105 (n = 12).
source: We did not observe the formation of tumours at any stage analysed (n = 12, Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is an observation from the postnatal YAP-TetO experiments.

claim: No lesions were observed in YAP-TetO animals when treating from P5.
source: Similarly, we did not observe the formation of lesions when treating from P5.
evidence: This is an observation from the postnatal YAP-TetO experiments.

claim: Elevation of YAP protein levels was confirmed in YAP-TetO animals following three weeks of doxycycline treatment (P42), displaying patchy accumulation.
source: Elevation of YAP protein levels was confirmed following three weeks of doxycycline treatment (P42), displaying patchy accumulation, likely a result of genetic recombination efficiencies (Figure 5B).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: There was robust elevation in the expression of transcriptional targets Cyr61 and Ctgf in YAP-TetO animals following treatment.
source: Consistent with pathway activation, there was robust elevation in the expression of transcriptional targets Cyr61 and Ctgf following treatment (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B)
evidence: This claim is supported by RNAscope data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Target expression in YAP-TetO animals was at significantly lower levels compared to Sox2CreERT2/+;Lats1fl/fl;Lats2fl/+ deletions.
source: however at significantly lower levels compared to Sox2CreERT2/+;Lats1fl/fl;Lats2fl/+ deletions (Figure 5—figure supplement 1E)
evidence: This claim is supported by quantified RNAscope data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1E.

claim: There was no elevation in phosphorylated inactive YAP in YAP-TetO animals.
source: and there was no elevation in phosphorylated inactive YAP (Figure 5B).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Immunofluorescence against SOX2 demonstrated a significant increase in the number of SOX2+ cells as a proportion of the anterior pituitary in YAP-TetO animals at P42 (18.0% compared to 12.1% in controls, p=0.0014).
source: Immunofluorescence against SOX2 demonstrated a significant increase in the number of SOX2+ cells as a proportion of the anterior pituitary (Figure 5B,F; 18.0% compared to 12.1% in controls, p=0.0014)
evidence: This claim is supported by quantified immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5B,F.

claim: The increase in the percentage of SOX2+ cells in YAP-TetO animals was maintained at all stages analysed.
source: This increase in the percentage of SOX2+ cells was maintained at all stages analysed (Figure 5F) and did not affect the overall morphology of the pituitary.
evidence: This claim is supported by quantified data shown in Figure 5F.

claim: At P42, a significant increase in proliferation among the SOX2+ pituitary stem cells was observed in YAP-TetO animals, from 3% in controls to 15% in mutants (p=0.027).
source: At P42 we observed a significant increase in proliferation among the SOX2+ pituitary stem cells from 3% in controls to 15% in mutants (p=0.027).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantified immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: SOX2+ cells make up 10% of all cycling cells (Ki-67+) in normal pituitaries, but this increased to 25% in YAP-TetO mutants.
source: SOX2+ cells make up 10% of all cycling cells (Ki-67%) in normal pituitaries, however in mutants this increased to 25%, suggesting a preferential expansion of the SOX2+ population, rather than an overall increase in proliferation (Figure 5C).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantified immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Longer treatment (P21 to P105) in YAP-TetO animals resulted in sporadic regions of expanded SOX2+ cells.
source: No additional marked differences were observed in samples analysed at P63 (6 weeks of treatment, n = 3), however longer treatment (P21 to P105) resulted in sporadic regions of expanded SOX2+ cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Regions of expanded SOX2+ cells in YAP-TetO animals did not express the commitment marker PIT1.
source: These regions did not express the commitment marker PIT1 and were identifiable by haematoxylin/eosin staining.
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence and histological data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1C.

claim: In contrast to tumour lesions generated following loss of LATS kinases, regions of expanded SOX2+ cells in YAP-TetO animals were not proliferative, were positive for pYAP and did not accumulate high levels of YAP/TAZ (n = 6 lesions).
source: In contrast to tumour lesions generated following loss of LATS kinases, these were not proliferative, were positive for pYAP and did not accumulate high levels of YAP/TAZ (n = 6 lesions).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1C.

claim: The sustained expression of constitutive active YAP can activate the proliferation of SOX2 stem cells, but in contrast to deletion of LATS1, this alone is not oncogenic.
source: Together these results suggest that the sustained expression of constitutive active YAP can activate the proliferation of SOX2 stem cells, but in contrast to deletion of LATS1, this alone is not oncogenic.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from comparing YAP-TetO and LATS deletion phenotypes.

claim: Immunofluorescence against total YAP protein confirmed restoration of the normal YAP expression pattern and levels after recovery in YAP-TetO animals.
source: Immunofluorescence against total YAP protein confirmed restoration of the normal YAP expression pattern and levels after recovery (Figure 5E)
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: mRNA in situ hybridisation detected a reduction in expression of YAP/TAZ targets Cyr61 and Ctgf after recovery in YAP-TetO animals.
source: and mRNA in situ hybridisation detected a reduction in expression of YAP/TAZ targets Cyr61 and Ctgf (Figure 5—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNAscope data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Following recovery from high levels of YAP, the number of SOX2+ cells reduced to comparable levels as in controls (around 10% of the total anterior pituitary).
source: Following recovery from high levels of YAP, the number of SOX2+ cells reduced to comparable levels as in controls (around 10% of the total anterior pituitary) (Figure 5E,F).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantified immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5E,F.

claim: The effects of YAP overexpression on the stem cell population are transient following three weeks of treatment.
source: This suggests that the effects of YAP overexpression on the stem cell population are transient following three weeks of treatment (Figure 5F).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the recovery experiments.

claim: Larger clones of SOX2 derivatives were observed at P63 in Sox2CreERT2/+;R26rtTA/mTmG;Col1a1tetO-Yap/+ animals compared to controls.
source: Larger clones of SOX2 derivatives were observed at P63 in Sox2CreERT2/+;R26rtTA/mTmG;Col1a1tetO-Yap/+ animals compared to controls, and these still contained SOX2+ cells (Figure 5H).
evidence: This claim is supported by lineage tracing data shown in Figure 5H.

claim: GFP+ derivatives of SOX2+ cells were detected which had differentiated into the three lineages (PIT1, SF1 and ACTH) following withdrawal in Sox2CreERT2/+;R26rtTA/mTmG;Col1a1tetO-Yap/+ animals.
source: Following withdrawal, we were able to detect GFP+ derivatives of SOX2+ cells, which had differentiated into the three lineages (PIT1, SF1 and ACTH, marking corticotrophs of the TPIT lineage) (Figure 5I).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5I.

claim: Sustained expression of YAP is sufficient to maintain the SOX2+ state and promote activation of normal SOX2+ pituitary stem cells in vivo, driving expansion of this population.
source: Taken together, these findings confirm that sustained expression of YAP is sufficient to maintain the SOX2+ state and promote activation of normal SOX2+ pituitary stem cells in vivo, driving expansion of this population.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the YAP-TetO and lineage tracing experiments.

claim: Regulation of LATS/YAP/TAZ signalling is essential during anterior pituitary development and can influence the activity of the stem/progenitor cell pool.
source: Here we establish that regulation of LATS/YAP/TAZ signalling is essential during anterior pituitary development and can influence the activity of the stem/progenitor cell pool.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion from all the experimental data.

claim: LATS kinases, mediated by YAP and TAZ, are responsible for controlling organ growth, promoting an undifferentiated state and repressing lineage commitment.
source: LATS kinases, mediated by YAP and TAZ, are responsible for controlling organ growth, promoting an undifferentiated state and repressing lineage commitment.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion from the LATS deletion experiments.

claim: Loss of both Lats1 and Lats2 leads to dramatic tissue overgrowth during gestation, revealing a function for these enzymes in restricting growth during pituitary development.
source: Loss of both Lats1 and Lats2, encoding potent tumour suppressors, leads to dramatic tissue overgrowth during gestation, revealing a function for these enzymes in restricting growth during pituitary development.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the embryonic LATS1/2 deletion experiments.

claim: The involvement of YAP/TAZ and dysfunction of the kinase cascade is emerging in multiple paediatric cancers, which are often developmental disorders.
source: The involvement of YAP/TAZ and dysfunction of the kinase cascade is emerging in multiple paediatric cancers, which are often developmental disorders (Ahmed et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Loss of LATS1 heterozygosity has been reported in a range of human tumours.
source: Loss of LATS1 heterozygosity has been reported in a range of human tumours (Lee et al., 1990; Chen et al., 2005; Theile et al., 1996; Mazurenko et al., 1999) leading to an increase in YAP/TAZ protein levels.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Previous global deletion of Lats1 in mice resulted in a variety of soft tissue sarcomas and stromal cell tumours.
source: Previous global deletion of Lats1 in mice resulted in a variety of soft tissue sarcomas and stromal cell tumours (St John et al., 1999).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: The anterior lobe of global Lats1 deletion mice appeared hyperplastic with poor endocrine cell differentiation leading to combined hormone deficiencies, but the presence of tumours was not noted.
source: The anterior lobe of these animals appeared hyperplastic with poor endocrine cell differentiation leading to combined hormone deficiencies, but the presence of tumours was not noted.
evidence: This is a reference to previous work on global Lats1 deletion.

claim: Loss of Lats1 alone is sufficient to drive anterior and intermediate lobe tumour formation.
source: We report that loss of Lats1 alone is sufficient to drive anterior and intermediate lobe tumour formation.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the current study's LATS1 deletion experiments.

claim: The tumour phenotype is accelerated following additional deletion of one copy of Lats2.
source: This phenotype is accelerated following additional deletion of one copy of Lats2.
evidence: This is an observation from comparing LATS1 single and LATS1/2 compound mutants.

claim: Phenotypically identical tumour lesions were generated when the genetic deletions were carried out embryonically in RP, or at postnatal stages.
source: Phenotypically identical tumour lesions were generated when the genetic deletions were carried out embryonically in RP, or at postnatal stages.
evidence: This is an observation from comparing Hesx1-Cre and Sox2-CreERT2 driven deletions.

claim: Regulation of LATS1/2 by kinases other than STK3/4 is possible in the pituitary.
source: Alternatively, regulation of LATS1/2 by kinases other than STK3/4 is possible in the pituitary, meaning deletion of Stk3/4 alone is insufficient to result in significant LATS function impairment.
evidence: This is speculation based on the lack of phenotype in STK3/4 deletion mutants.

claim: Similar situations where LATS function without STK3/4 have been reported in other organs.
source: Similar situations have been reported in other organs where LATS are functioning (Hu et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: The resulting non-secreting tumours in the mouse models are composed predominantly of SOX2+ stem cells and display signs of squamous differentiation.
source: The resulting non-secreting tumours in our mouse models are composed predominantly of SOX2+ stem cells and display signs of squamous differentiation.
evidence: This is a summary of the tumour characterization data.

claim: Rare cases of squamous cell carcinoma have been reported as primary pituitary tumours.
source: Rare cases of squamous cell carcinoma have been reported as primary pituitary tumours (Saeger et al., 2007), but more frequently, arising within cysts that are normally non-neoplastic epithelial malformations (Lewis et al., 1983; O'Neill et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous clinical reports.

claim: In the embryonic YAP-TetO model, cysts phenocopying Rathke's cleft cyst develop by postnatal stages.
source: In the embryonic YAP-TetO model, where constitutive active YAP (S127A) was expressed during pituitary development, cysts phenocopying Rathke's cleft cyst, develop by postnatal stages.
evidence: This is a summary of the YAP-TetO phenotype.

claim: Target elevation is not as high in YAP-TetO pituitaries as following the deletion of LATS1/2, indicating that signalling levels are likely to be critical for progression between these phenotypes.
source: Target elevation is not as high in YAP-TetO pituitaries, as following the deletion of LATS1/2, indicating that signalling levels are likely to be critical for progression between these phenotypes.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from comparing target gene expression levels between models.

claim: The tumours generated in LATS1/2 mouse models fit the histopathological profile of human pituitary carcinomas.
source: Although human pituitary carcinomas are only diagnosed as such after metastasis, the tumours generated in our LATS1/2 mouse models fit their histopathological profile.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the histopathological characterization of the tumours.

claim: Genetic lineage tracing identified SOX2+ cells as the cell of origin of the tumours.
source: Genetic lineage tracing identified SOX2+ cells as the cell of origin of the tumours; this observation could have ramifications regarding involvement of the LATS/YAP/TAZ pathway in the establishment or progression of human pituitary tumours composed of uncommitted cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the lineage tracing experiments.

claim: In cancer stem cells of osteosarcoma and glioblastoma, SOX2 antagonises upstream Hippo activators, leading to enhanced YAP function.
source: In cancer stem cells of osteosarcoma and glioblastoma, SOX2 antagonises upstream Hippo activators, leading to enhanced YAP function (Basu-Roy et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Enhanced expression of YAP/TAZ was recently reported in a range of non-functioning human pituitary tumours, compared to functioning adenomas.
source: We recently reported enhanced expression of YAP/TAZ in a range of non-functioning human pituitary tumours, compared to functioning adenomas, and that Lats1 knock-down in GH3 pituitary mammosomatotropinoma cells results in repression of the Gh and Prl promoters (Xekouki et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to the authors' recent work.

claim: YAP/TAZ are likely to function both to promote the maintenance of an active pituitary stem cell state as well as to inhibit differentiation.
source: Therefore, YAP/TAZ, perhaps in a positive feedback loop with SOX2, are likely to function both to promote the maintenance of an active pituitary stem cell state as well as to inhibit differentiation.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data and previous literature.

claim: Expression of constitutively active YAP (S127A) is sufficient to push SOX2+ pituitary stem cells into an activated state, leading to expansion of the stem cell cohort.
source: By dissecting the downstream requirement for YAP in pituitary regulation by the LATS/YAP/TAZ axis, we found that expression of constitutively active YAP (S127A) is sufficient to push SOX2+ pituitary stem cells into an activated state, leading to expansion of the stem cell cohort (see Model, Figure 6).
evidence: This is a conclusion from the YAP-TetO experiments, illustrated in the model in Figure 6.

claim: YAP has previously been indicated to promote the stem cell state in other tissues, for example pancreas, neurons and mammary glands.
source: YAP has previously been indicated to promote the stem cell state in other tissues, for example pancreas, neurons and mammary glands (Panciera et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: YAP activation does not fully recapitulate the LATS deletion phenotypes, as it did not lead to the formation of tumours during the time course of YAP activation (12 weeks).
source: However, this does not fully recapitulate the LATS deletion phenotypes, as it did not lead to the formation of tumours during the time course of YAP activation (12 weeks).
evidence: This is an observation from comparing YAP-TetO and LATS deletion phenotypes.

claim: Initiation of tumourigenesis may be associated with levels of signalling rising above a threshold.
source: Interestingly, since the levels of target activation are significantly greater in Lats1/2 deletions that in YAP-TetO activation, initiation of tumourigenesis may be associated with levels of signalling rising above a threshold.
evidence: This is speculation based on the difference in target gene expression levels between models.

claim: The temporal control of expressing the mutation is critical, as seen in other tumour models.
source: However, the temporal control of expressing the mutation is critical, as seen in other tumour models (Han et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous work on tumour models.

claim: YAP has an isolated role in promoting the expansion of the SOX2+ stem cell pool and restoring their proliferative potential to levels akin to the most active state during postnatal pituitary growth.
source: Instead, the findings identify an isolated role for YAP in promoting the expansion of the SOX2+ stem cell pool and restoring their proliferative potential to levels akin to the most active state during postnatal pituitary growth.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the YAP-TetO experiments.

claim: Activity of YAP/TAZ is reduced in dense tissues, resulting in a decrease in stemness.
source: Activity of YAP/TAZ is reduced in dense tissues, resulting in a decrease in stemness.
evidence: This is established knowledge about YAP/TAZ regulation.

claim: One mechanism through which YAP/TAZ activity is reduced in dense tissues is by crosstalk with other signalling pathways regulating stem cell fate.
source: One mechanism through which this is achieved is by crosstalk with other signalling pathways regulating stem cell fate (Papaspyropoulos et al., 2018; Heallen et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: A decrease in YAP/TAZ activity removes inhibition on Notch signalling, resulting in higher levels of differentiation and a drop in stem cell potential.
source: For example, a decrease in YAP/TAZ activity removes inhibition on Notch signalling, resulting in higher levels of differentiation and a drop in stem cell potential (Totaro et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: In the pituitary, Notch plays a role in the maintenance of the SOX2 stem cell compartment and is involved in regulating differentiation.
source: In the pituitary, Notch plays a role in the maintenance of the SOX2 stem cell compartment and is involved in regulating differentiation (Zhu et al., 2015; Nantie et al., 2014; Cheung et al., 2013; Batchuluun et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous work on Notch in the pituitary.

claim: The findings highlight roles for LATS/YAP/TAZ in the regulation of pituitary stem cells, where fine-tuning of their expression can make the difference between physiological stem cell re-activation and tumourigenesis.
source: In summary, our findings highlight roles for LATS/YAP/TAZ in the regulation of pituitary stem cells, where fine-tuning of their expression can make the difference between physiological stem cell re-activation and tumourigenesis, of relevance to other organs.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion from all the experimental data.

claim: This axis is involved in the control of cell fate commitment, regulation of regenerative potential and promotion of tumourigenesis.
source: We reveal this axis is involved in the control of cell fate commitment, regulation of regenerative potential and promotion of tumourigenesis.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion from all the experimental data.

claim: These findings can aid in the design of treatments against pituitary tumours and in regenerative medicine approaches targeting the regulation of endogenous stem cells.
source: These findings can aid in the design of treatments against pituitary tumours and in regenerative medicine approaches targeting the regulation of endogenous stem cells.
evidence: This is a statement about potential applications of the findings.
